Ella —

Thanks for the clear questions and the volume file. Short answers up front:

- Redwood supports both marginal and blended semantics; default commercial practice is marginal (you pay the marginal rate for tokens within each band) but we can offer a blended/true-up hybrid for committed programs.
- Clawbacks are negotiable. We typically offer a capped clawback for pilots, and an annual true-up for multi-month commitments.
- Region consolidation is supported on invoices if you opt into our consolidated billing (adds a small reconciliation lag).

I'll loop Ben (pricing) and Laura (manager approvals) to propose a concrete ladder and clawback cap. If helpful, we can offer a capped-clawback + carryforward credit that limits retroactive liability to one quarter.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to share a draft ladder (marginal vs blended scenarios).
2) Internal review (legal/procurement) before we produce the formal SOW language.
3) 30-minute call this week to align on clawback tolerance.

Are you available Thursday 10/7 10:00am PT?

Thanks Ella / Jonas —

Attaching a draft ladder that shows three variants: pure marginal, pure blended effective-rate, and a hybrid we call "tilted-blend" (blends at breakpoints but caps cell-level clawbacks). Key callouts inside the sheet:
- Breakpoints at 0-500M, 500M-2B, 2B+.
- Marginal rates reduce per-band; blended produces a single effective $/k token.
- Hybrid: we let marginal math apply for actual billing but cap the max retroactive clawback per quarter to 20% of the quarter's cost. Excess is carried forward as credits.

Why hybrid? It preserves volume-incentive signaling for you while making financial exposure bounded for Stratus. If this aligns, legal can translate "cap and carryforward" into SOW language (sample clause included).

Attachment: redwood_proposed_ladder_v2.xlsx (sheets: ladder, examples, SOW_clause)

Ben

Ella —

Thanks for the clarifying questions and for the pilot openness. Summary / agreed path forward: 

1) We'll run Q4 as a 90-day pilot under the hybrid "tilted-blend" ladder (attached PDF proposal).
2) Clawback cap: 20% of quarterly invoice by default; reduces to 15% if Stratus converts to a 12-month commit at >= 750M tokens/mo average. Cap is calculated on the gross invoice dollars for that quarter (not incremental savings).
3) Invoice worked example: Ben attached a 3-month spike scenario (see proposed_ladder sheet). We bill monthly at marginal math; any clawback owed is netted and capped at quarter close and excess becomes a credit carried forward up to 2 quarters.
4) Token counting: Redwood counts at request+response tokenization (pre-compression). We'll include a short technical appendix in the SOW.
5) Next operational steps: Jonas to send SOW language + DocuSign; legal/procurement to review. Expect a DocuSign send by COB 10/13.
